text: This capstone follows one request from a fictional company, Thornbury Cycle Supply Co., all the way through to three finished deliverables. Leadership wants a Quarterly Business Review package, built on the real AdventureWorks2012 sample database.

That one request actually breaks into three different jobs. Executives want an interactive Power BI dashboard they can click through live. The Board wants a polished Tableau deck, built for presenting. Finance wants an Excel workbook they can audit themselves with their own formulas. Three audiences, three real tools, three different jobs-to-be-done.

The only way to build three deliverables that agree with each other is to build them all on top of the same underlying numbers. That's why this capstone builds one T-SQL warehouse first, with an automated Python data-quality layer underneath it, and only then builds Power BI, Tableau, and Excel on top — each reading the warehouse directly, never reading each other.
Next lesson turns this plain-English plan into the real, named pieces you're actually going to build — the warehouse schema, the validation script, and all three front-ends.
